questions.question: How should the pytest-gremlins pin move?

options.label: >=1.11.0,<1.12 now (Recommended)
options.description: Picks up the timeout fix and #568 today. Needs a full mutation.yml dispatch on the branch before merge, as the pyproject comment requires. 1.11.1 is then a same-minor bump later.

options.label: Wait for 1.11.1, then >=1.11.1,<1.12
options.description: One validation dispatch covers both releases (__init__ gremlins, parametrize-id fix, -p no:xdist crash). Delay is unknown, since 1.11.1 isn't on PyPI yet.

options.label: Leave >=1.10.1,<1.11
options.description: No work now. Scores can stay inflated by unconfirmed timeout kills.

questions.question: What should happen to the argv-forwarding workaround?

options.label: Keep it, update comments (Recommended)
options.description: Keep argv forwarding and its guard tests. Rewrite the mutation.yml and run_mutate.py comments: the pre-scan bug is fixed upstream in 1.11.0 (#568), and argv stays because it's explicit and works on every version.

options.label: Keep it unchanged
options.description: Leave the comments as they are. They'll describe a bug that no longer exists once the floor is 1.11.

options.label: Remove it
options.description: Allow flags in PYTEST_ADDOPTS again. Saves little and drops a guard that works on every version.

questions.question: How should the ERROR blind spot in mutation_report.classify_scopes be handled?

options.label: Fix in the same PR (Recommended)
options.description: Classify error>0 as its own non-ok verdict and surface timeout_warning in the issue body. This ships with the bump, so 1.11's new ERRORs are visible in the validation dispatch.

options.label: Separate backlog item
options.description: Do the bump only and open a BUG item for the classifier. Until it lands, ERRORs from the validation dispatch only show in the table columns.

options.label: Ignore
options.description: Treat ERROR as acceptable noise. A scope can then read 'ok' while its timeouts are unconfirmed.

questions.question: How should the ERROR blind spot in mutation_report.classify_scopes be handled?
When a scope has ERRORs (most likely unconfirmed timeouts on 1.11), what should the rolling [mutation] issue do?

options.label: Advisory, own section (Recommended)
options.description: New 'errors' verdict, never 'ok'. It gets its own section in the issue body and table, with the plugin's timeout_warning text, but does not open or keep open the issue, like survivors. Avoids an issue that never closes while the ~15 slow scopes are tuned.

options.label: Opens the issue
options.description: ERRORs count as harness-class, so the issue opens and the run reports unhealthy until mutant_timeout or the slow tests are fixed. Strictest, but the first 1.11 run almost certainly opens it.

options.label: Opens only on timeout_warning
options.description: Unconfirmed timeouts (a config problem with a clear fix) open the issue. Other ERRORs, such as 1.11.1's 'no runnable selected test', stay advisory. More precise, but adds a second rule to maintain.

questions.question: The pin policy needs a full mutation.yml dispatch on 1.11 before merge (run 47 took about 2.5 h on 76 legs). How should it be run, and how should mutant_timeout be handled?

options.label: Dispatch, then tune (Recommended)
options.description: I dispatch mutation.yml on gremlins-1-11 after the classifier fix lands. If ERRORs show up, I set mutant_timeout in [tool.pytest-gremlins] from the measured test runtimes and record both runs in the trace.

options.label: Dispatch, no tuning
options.description: Run it once, record the result, and keep the 30 s default. Any ERRORs stay visible as a finding for a follow-up item.

options.label: You dispatch it
options.description: I push everything and stop. You trigger the run and tell me the run id, and I analyze it.

What should happen to the accidentally opened PR #1082?

options.label: Keep, mark as draft (Recommended)
options.description: I convert it to a draft and fix the escaped title now. After run 48 and the mutant_timeout tuning, I fill the body from the PR template (as /pr would), run its gates and mark it ready. Same PR number, and CI already runs.

options.label: Close it
options.description: I close #1082. Once the work is done, /pr opens a new PR with a new number. #1082 stays visible as closed.

options.label: Leave as is
options.description: No change. It stays open and ready-for-review with the commit-message body until I update it after run 48.
